approachQuestion.prompt:
Smallest warranty covering each reading

Each of n warranty records covers a closed integer serial-number range [start,end]. For each of q serial-number queries x, return the smallest range length end−start+1 among records containing x, or −1 if none do. Records and queries are unsorted and immutable. All queries are available before answering, and results must be returned in original query order.

Input: records=[[1,10],[4,6],[8,9]], queries=[5,8,11,5]
Output: [3,2,-1,3]

Input: records=[[2,2]], queries=[2,3]
Output: [1,-1]

Constraints: 1 ≤ n,q ≤ 200000; integer endpoints satisfy 0 ≤ start ≤ end ≤ 1000000000; query values are in the same coordinate range. Use comparison-based sorting and priority queues. Choose the best worst-case time among the listed methods.

options.text: Sort copied records by start and indexed query copies by x. For each query in order, insert all records with start ≤ x into a min-heap keyed by length. While the heap minimum ends before x, remove it. Return the minimum length or −1, storing it at the query’s original index.
options.feedback: All eligible starts have entered the heap. Expired nonminimum records may remain, but cannot spoil the answer: an expired record is removed if it reaches the minimum, and any valid minimum is no longer than every other candidate.

options.text: Use the ordered query sweep but keep records in a heap keyed only by end; after dropping expired minima, return the length of the earliest-ending record.
options.feedback: For records [[0,5],[4,6]] and query 4, earliest end chooses length 6, but the range [4,6] has the smaller length 3.

options.text: Use a length heap and insert by start during the query sweep, but never remove records whose end is before the current query.
options.feedback: For records [[1,1],[0,10]] and queries [1,5], the singleton is valid only for the first query. Keeping it returns 1 instead of 11 for query 5.

options.text: For every query, test every record for containment and take the minimum length of the containing records.
options.feedback: This is correct but repeats all record checks for every query. Offline ordering lets starts be added once and expired candidates be discarded lazily.

feedback.reason: Maintain the smallest active covering interval with an offline sweep and safe lazy expiration.
details: Copy records and indexed queries, sort each by its sweep coordinate using iterative bottom-up merge sort and reusable buffers. Use an iterative binary heap keyed by (length,end), preallocated for n records. Each record is inserted once and removed at most once. Store answers in the returned array.

Insert warranties once their start is at or before the query. Remove expired heap tops before answering; an expired non-top can wait until it reaches the top. Scatter answers back using original query indices.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For offline-shortest-active, include all sorting, heap operations and query scans. Count record/query copies, buffers and heap, but exclude the returned q answers. Choose the tightest standard worst-case pair in n,q.
constraints: Analyze only the named method. Count all temporary arrays and the call stack; exclude the supplied input and returned output. Numeric comparisons, assignments and arithmetic take constant time, with no overflow.
No hashing or amortized data structure is used. All loops and binary searches are iterative; there is no recursive stack.

options.text: Time O((n+q) log(n+q)), auxiliary space O(n+q)
Time O((n+q) log(n+q)), auxiliary space O(n)

feedback.reason: Sort records and queries; each record enters and leaves the heap at most once.
details: Two sorts require O(n log n+q log q), which is O((n+q) log(n+q)). At most n insertions and n removals each cost O(log n), and queries add linear scanning work. Copies and sorting buffers total O(n+q), and the heap uses O(n). Preallocated iterative structures avoid amortization and recursion assumptions.
Offline indexed query sort; iterative comparison merge sorts and binary heap; returned answers excluded.
“Time O(nq), auxiliary space O(n+q)”: All record-query pairs are not tested. The sweep inserts each record once and lazily removes it at most once.
“Time O((n+q) log(n+q)), auxiliary space O(n)”: The indexed query copy and its merge buffer each depend on q. Excluding the returned answers does not exclude these separate working arrays.
“Time O(n+q), auxiliary space O(n+q)”: Comparison sorting and heap updates are required; the linear sweep alone omits those costs.
